Besuch.et: From Middle High German besuoch (“test; interest (of borrowed money); right to use a place as pasture grounds”), from Old High German besuoch (“temptation”). Compare German Low German Besök/Besöök, Beseik. By surface analysis, be- + suchen.

besudeln.et: From Middle High German besudeln, besodeln, besodelen, equivalent to be- + Sudel (“puddle; muck”), from Middle Low German sudde (“swamp; marsh”). Akin to Middle High German sutte (“puddle; mudhole”), Old English ġesyd (“wallowing hole”).

s: Wir haben heute unsere Mama in der Seniorenwohnanlage besucht.

besuchen.et: From Middle High German besuochen (“to seek, use, visit, investigate”), from Old High German bisuohhen (“to examine, check, try, inquire”), from Proto-West Germanic *bisōkijan. By surface analysis, be- + suchen. Cognate with Dutch bezoeken (“to visit, see”), S…
